name: The Broken Reliquary

detectability.signature: Persistent subspace harmonics bleeding through into normal space, detectable as oscillating tachyon bursts on long-range arrays

proximity: Navigation systems report contradictory positional data as local spacetime geometry warps
Faint translucent architecture becomes visible at the periphery of vision, vanishing when observed directly
Communication signals experience unpredictable delays of 2-15 seconds
contact: Hull integrity sensors trigger false readings as the boundary between realspace and subspace thins
Crew members report vivid spatial disorientation, perceiving corridors and rooms that do not exist on their vessel
Physical objects left unattended may shift position by several centimeters between observations
prolonged_exposure: Subspace bleedthrough becomes severe enough to physically displace small objects into adjacent dimensional layers
Crew experience persistent hallucinations of vast ruined halls extending in impossible directions from bulkheads
Structural microfractures accumulate in hull plating as material is stressed across dimensional boundaries

age: Unknown — subspace dating methods return contradictory results spanning millions of years

behavior.cycle: Irregular expansions every 47-53 hours, each lasting approximately 6 hours

phenomena: Ghostly outlines of immense columned halls and shattered domes flicker in and out of visibility within the breach zone
Debris that enters the anomaly occasionally reappears days later, aged by centuries and covered in unfamiliar mineral deposits
Localized gravity inversions create pockets where objects fall upward for minutes at a time
Radio telescopes trained on the breach detect faint, structured signals that resemble no known language or natural emission
hazards: Uncontrolled dimensional displacement can strand vessels or crew in subspace pockets with no clear exit vector
Pulsation events dramatically expand the breach radius by up to 40%, catching ships that believed themselves at safe distance
Accumulated subspace stress on hull materials can cause catastrophic decompression without warning
opportunities: Subspace mineral deposits recovered from displaced debris include exotic crystalline structures with potential superconducting applications
The breach may serve as an unstable but navigable shortcut through subspace if its pulsation cycle can be reliably predicted
Study of the anomaly's structured signals could advance understanding of subspace topology and inter-dimensional physics
known_incidents: The survey vessel INS Cartographer entered during a pulsation event in 2847 and was recovered three weeks later, its crew aged by eleven years and its cargo hold containing stone fragments of clearly artificial origin
A Merchant Guild convoy lost two freighters to sudden dimensional displacement in 2901; one was recovered in subspace after a costly rescue operation, the other remains missing
description: The Broken Reliquary manifests as a vast, shimmering wound in the fabric of realspace, its boundaries defined by the ghostly silhouettes of impossible architecture. Enormous columned halls, fractured domes, and crumbling archways flicker at the edges of perception, rendered in translucent light that seems to bleed from somewhere behind the visible spectrum. The breach stretches across nearly a third of an astronomical unit, its irregular shape shifting slowly like the outline of a ruin settling further into collapse.

During its erratic pulsation cycles, the Reliquary expands outward in surges that warp local spacetime and blur the boundary between dimensions. Ships caught in these expansions report severe navigational failures, spatial hallucinations, and the physical displacement of unsecured objects. The effects intensify dramatically at the core, where subspace and realspace overlap so thoroughly that the laws of physics become suggestions rather than rules.

No civilization has claimed responsibility for the Reliquary, and its age remains a subject of fierce academic debate. The structured signals emanating from deep within the breach suggest artificial origin, yet subspace dating methods return results spanning millions of years — far predating any known spacefaring species. Some xenoarchaeologists theorize that the anomaly is the dimensional footprint of a structure that existed in a now-collapsed layer of subspace, its ruins bleeding through into our reality like a scar that refuses to heal.

The Broken Reliquary remains an active navigational hazard and a source of intense scientific interest. Several research stations maintain observation posts at safe distance, though the definition of 'safe' has been revised outward three times in the past century. Salvage teams occasionally brave the outer reaches during quiescent periods, recovering exotic materials and fragments of alien stonework that command extraordinary prices on the xenoarchaeological market. The breach shows no signs of closing, and some models suggest it may be slowly widening.
